sections.heading: Start
paragraphs: Choose Signal Stack in AfterHours, review the controls, and start Standard Transmission. The matrix begins immediately after the loading sequence.

sections.heading: Controls
paragraphs: Move packets with Left and Right. Down performs a soft drop; Space performs a hard drop. Up or X rotates clockwise, Z rotates counterclockwise, and C holds one packet per placement.
Escape pauses play. The controls screen always shows the bindings active on the current host.

sections.heading: Rules
paragraphs: Arrange four-cell signal packets in the 10 by 20 visible matrix. Completed horizontal channels clear from the matrix. Five upcoming packets are shown, and the packet sequence uses a shuffled seven-packet bag.
Transmission rate advances primarily every ten cleared channels. A run ends when a new packet cannot enter or when occupied cells lock in the hidden region.

sections.heading: Scoring
paragraphs: Channel clears, phase rotations, signal chains, sustained transmissions, soft drops, and hard drops contribute to the score. Clearing the complete matrix awards a zero-state bonus.

sections.heading: Accessibility
paragraphs: Packet shapes and labels carry critical state in addition to color. High Contrast and color-safe palettes, reduced motion, reduced flashing, disabled shake, and disabled browser CRT effects do not make a score noncanonical.

sections.heading: Archive note
paragraphs: Frankenberg Logic Bureau developed Signal Stack with technology from Vranidoll Signal Works. Sara Circuitworks published the commercial release.

sections.heading: Start
paragraphs: Choose Loopback in AfterHours or launch Quick Circuit directly. The route begins moving to the right with three integrity points and a two-minute service window.

sections.heading: Controls
paragraphs: Steer in four directions with the directional controls. A route cannot reverse directly into itself. Escape pauses play.

sections.heading: Rules
paragraphs: Collect the active payload while avoiding walls and the existing route. Paired network ports move the route head to the matching port without changing its direction.
A collision removes one integrity point, resets the route, and grants a short visible recovery interval. The service timer continues. The run ends when integrity reaches zero or the timer expires.

sections.heading: Scoring
paragraphs: Each payload is worth 100 points multiplied by the current port multiplier. Port traversal raises the next-payload multiplier up to four times; collecting a payload resets it. Completing the service window adds 500 points for each remaining integrity point.

sections.heading: Accessibility
paragraphs: The route, payload, ports, hazards, recovery state, and integrity use distinct symbols and labels as well as color. Keyboard and hardware-styled touch controls enter the same game actions.

sections.heading: Archive note
paragraphs: Noah Arc Labs began Loopback as a network-routing utility. Reçica Computer Works distributed it as fast bundled software for the DRX-90.
